title: Spatially periodic initial conditions always give repetitive behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Spatially periodic initial conditions always give repetitive behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In any cellular automaton, an initial condition consisting of a fixed block of n cells repeated forever leads to repetitive behavior with period at most 2^n, since each block evolves like a finite cyclic system.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: in any cellular automaton it is inevitable that initial conditions which consist just of a fixed block of cells repeated forever will lead to simple repetitive behavior.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Special Initial Conditions” (from p. 266), p. 267. Scope: all cellular automata with spatially periodic initial conditions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.99

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Under the binary-cell context, the claim follows immediately from finiteness and determinism. The proof covers every cellular-automaton rule and does not require empirical sampling.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reduce a spatially n-periodic binary configuration to a deterministic map on its 2^n possible blocks. The orbit must eventually cycle with temporal period at most 2^n; a nonbinary alphabet replaces the bound by q^n.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The numerical 2^n bound assumes two cell states.

The trajectory can have a transient before repetition.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 1.0
data adequacy: 0.98
discriminating power: 0.98
operationalizability: 0.97
data existence: 1.0

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The argument in the text is a complete proof: spatial period n plus a deterministic local rule reduces each block to a finite ring of 2^n states, which must cycle. It applies to every cellular automaton, which is the stated scope, and the counting step is immediate. Concrete rules can be spot-checked in Golly, but the general claim does not depend on those runs.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A spatially periodic seed of period n makes every length-n block identical, so one block evolves as a 2^n-state deterministic system and the temporal period is at most 2^n. A cellular automaton and a repeated block whose evolution never cycled within that bound would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The bound is an upper limit, not the period that a given block actually attains.

The factor 2^n is for two colors; the same argument with k colors gives k^n.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.98
analysis feasibility: 0.95
data existence: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.98
discriminating power: 0.95

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: For every cellular automaton tested and every block of n cells repeated forever as the initial condition, the evolution is eventually time-periodic with period at most k^n (k = number of colours; 2^n for two colours), and the infinite repeated-block configuration evolves exactly as a cyclic ring of n cells.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py treats a block of n cells repeated forever as an n-cell ring, builds the ring's transition map on all k^n states for each rule and computes the eventual period of every state's orbit from the functional graph (cycle detection by in-degree peeling). Families: all 256 ECA for n = 1..12 (2,096,640 rule-block pairs), all 2187 three-colour totalistic rules for n = 1..6 (2,388,204 pairs, bound 3^n), and 500 seeded random range-2 binary rules for n = 1..10 (1,023,000 pairs). It then checks the reduction itself: for all 256 ECA and all 32,256 blocks of n = 1..6, a line of repeated copies of the block is evolved for 2*2^n steps and its central copy compared cell by cell with the ring evolution (15,845,376 cells). Run time about 18 s.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: (1) across all (rule, block) pairs enumerated, 100% have eventual temporal period <= k^n (zero violations); (2) for every (rule, block) pair in the equivalence sample, the central block of a long line made of repeated copies of the block evolves identically to the n-cell ring for all simulated steps (zero mismatching cells).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: any (rule, block) pair whose eventual period exceeds k^n, or any pair for which the repeated-block line evolution differs from the ring evolution inside the region unaffected by the line's ends.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: fraction of (rule, block) pairs whose eventual temporal period is <= k^n

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: exact (exhaustive within each family; the range-2 family is a seeded sample of 500 of 2^32 rules)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Initial conditions which consist just of a fixed block of cells repeated forever' is a spatially n-periodic configuration on the infinite line. 'Simple repetitive behavior' is read as eventual time-periodicity of the configuration, and the stated bound 2^n is read, following Wolfram's own reasoning and the assessors, as k^n for k colours (2^n in the two-colour case the text has in mind). 'Any cellular automaton' cannot be enumerated, so three families are tested: all 256 elementary rules exhaustively (n = 1..12), all 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic rules (n = 1..6, bound 3^n), and a fixed-seed random sample of 500 two-colour range-2 (5-neighbour) rules out of 2^32 (n = 1..10). The reduction 'each block evolves like a finite cyclic system' is tested separately by simulating the actual repeated-block line and comparing it with the ring.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
All 256 ECA x all 2^n blocks of n = 1..12 cells repeated forever (generated by analysis.py)

All 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic rules x all 3^n blocks of n = 1..6 cells (generated by analysis.py)

500 random two-colour range-2 rules (5-cell neighbourhood, 2^32 rule space; numpy default_rng seed 20261031) x all 2^n blocks of n = 1..10 (generated by analysis.py)

All 256 ECA x all blocks of n = 1..6 cells, repeated on a long line, compared with the ring (generated by analysis.py)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The claim quantifies over all cellular automata; three rule families (one exhaustive over all 256 elementary rules, one exhaustive over all 2187 three-colour totalistic rules, one a 500-rule sample of range-2 rules) were tested, and the general statement rests on the finite-state argument that the line-vs-ring check confirms empirically for the elementary rules.

The bound k^n is attained only in degenerate cases (n = 1, rules that cycle through every state); for n >= 2 the overwhelming majority of periods are below k^n / 10 (see the histogram), so the bound is loose but never violated.

Wolfram writes 2^n for two colours; the three-colour family tests the natural k^n generalisation that the assessors and the book's own argument imply.
